findingsForTheLedger: The startup task leaves no durable record of its result: after a restart nobody can say whether it restored the entry, found it there, or failed. (The application does notice a missing entry, by using the profile.)
An ordinary user cannot read the task (definition, last run, last result): the application can tell "there" from "not there" and nothing more.
A fast startup (boot type 0x1) does not run the task; the entry survives with the restored kernel session. To be covered by the reboot matrix, with a hibernation resume (0x2).
C:\ProgramData\NexusSandbox\bin holds about 200 copies of the launcher, one per build of the development tree: nothing removes the old ones.
The machine still lists "NEXUS 0.7.0" among installed programs (an earlier installer test): to be accounted for by the installer lifecycle.

The installed copy of restore-canonicalization.ps1 differs from the repository in line endings only (same text); a hash comparison by the application would have to allow for it or the setup must copy bytes as they are.
verdict: PASS: the reboot recovery of v0.8.0 worked with no user interruption. Two questions (restored or persistent) cannot be answered from what 0.8 records.
